pr_title: RFC + executor: Support global memory tracker
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!
PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
UCP: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/15407
Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/15407

Support Global Memory tracker to control the memory usage and kill the current session's if the global memory usage in tracker exceeds the limit.


### What is changed and how it works?
Currently, we have already support the Global Disk Tracker for `Executor` And the Support of Global memory Tracker for `Executor` is quite likely the same.
 
## Proposal

see https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/17103



### Related changes

- PR to update `pingcap/docs`/`pingcap/docs-cn`:
- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test


### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

 - Support Global Memory tracker for tidb-server

issue_context.title: UCP: make memory usage of executors fit global memory limitation
issue_context.body:
## Description

Now nearly every executor has been tracking its memory usage using [`memory.Tracker`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/pingcap/tidb/util/memory?tab=doc#Tracker). And here's a `max-memory` configuration but is not taking effect on executors.
```
# Max memory size to use, 0 use the total usable memory in the machine.
max-memory = 0
```

If the memory usage of a SQL is exceeded by the global memory limitation, we need either,
1) kill this SQL
2) kill the SQL which is consuming the most memory

Tips:
1) We may need to maintain a global `memory.Tracker`
2) `max-memory` is currently used by PrepareCache, we may need to find a way to re-implement it.

* 3488

review_comments: If the item in the cache is deleted by LRU replacement, or by cache invalidation, I suppose this memory release would be reflected in the profile of this function name?
Right. The heap profile 's flat value showed the current heap usage referenced for the given function. If the cached is released, it would be reflected in the next scraping result.
How expensive is this function call? would it impact the performance of other goroutines on this tidb-server evidently?

This function scrape the heap information in a goroutine without any mutex/resource contention. And 791af28 is the same as c1bee54, we have run tpcc test for 791af28 and result showed that it won't affect the query tps/qps.
Why don't we lock the parent in functions like `Consume`, instead, to lock it here?
Lock `parent` is my first trial when I found the data race error, maybe adding lock in the `Consume` function is also enough. But the tpcc test result already seems ok if we lock `parent` here.
Better to add a test case covering `SimpleLRUCache.Put` interface and check `GlobalLRUMemUsageTracker` tracks reasonable memory it consumes.
